text.p: UnionAmerica Holdings Plc chairman Philip Marcell said he was comfortable with analysts' fourth quarter earnings estimate of $0.60 a share.
He said he also was comfortable with the First Call consensus estimate of $2.25 a share for 1996.
Marcell, speaking to Reuters in an interview, also said he was "pretty confident" the company could achieve return on equity in excess of 15 percent in 1997, despite the competitive environment.

Marcell, who is scheduled to give a presentation Thursday at a Merrill Lynch insurance conference in New York, said the London-based company is scheduled to release fourth quarter earnings in mid-March.

Although competition is currently putting pressure on prices, Marcell said he believes the environment will improve by the end of 1998, when insurers will be forced to raise rates after suffering losses from the soft prices.
"I don't believe the environment will be as tough as it is today, say by the time you get to the end of '98," Marcell said.
The turnaround will come "mainly because I think pricing is getting very close to the edge now," he said.
Although UnionAmerica is based in London, about 86 percent of its business comes from the United States, with the remainder coming from Europe and Australia, Marcell said.
